export_checks: 92 solver summaries across the two run roots, 23 per level, no task twice; the quota-stopped Medium cellarcore attempt and the transport-stopped High snapcore attempt hold no summary and are not part of the population

every run is muse-code:muse-wonder-full-1.0-contributor at its requested level; Low and 21 Medium runs on Muse Code 1.4.6 from bench/2026-10-13-musewonder-full-v2-low, the last two Medium runs, High and Extra-high on 1.4.9 from bench/2026-10-16-musewonder-full-149, every source block clean, every task hash equal to the frozen suite lock
every integrity audit: no web, no benchmark data or answer-key paths, nothing outside the workspace but Muse Code's own per-run session folder
each run's token totals equal its trace's muse_usage record; reminder-observer usage appears only on 1.4.9 runs, only on muse-spark-1.3, and equals the population record
the four population records' hashes equal the ones frozen in their protocols, and every judged run's summary hash equals its manifest entry
v3.26 binds GPT-6.1 Sol's v3.25 protocol, calibration and manifest by hash; v3.26.1 to v3.26.3 bind both exam verdicts by hash and plan no calibration calls
rubric, prompts, schemas, seed, repeats, gate allowance, weights, retry rule and control hashes are identical in v3.25 and every v3.26 round
both judges passed calibration with no failing gate and no allowance used; no reviewer fallbacks in any round
per-row Code quality and both combined scores recomputed and matched to the frozen summaries; Low, High and Extra-high cell means and standard errors matched to their round's summary
combined score, its standard error, the timeouts-as-0 figure, functional score, tasks passed, minutes, cost and each judge's reviewed score per level matched to the harness card
the rates applied equal the pricing check; no dashes or host paths in exported text
limits: Muse Wonder Full is judged by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, not by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 like the other Frontier v4 columns except Grok 4.7 (Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol): Muse Spark 1.3 is a Meta model and is not neutral for a Meta submission. Scores from different panels are not calibrated against each other.
Claude Opus 5.5 rates Muse Wonder Full's reviewed Code quality about 17 points below GPT-6.1 Sol at every level. The published score is their mean; combined_single_judge gives each judge alone.
Claude Opus 5.5 judged these runs and is also a compared model on the harness card and the board; its own column comes from its own round, judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6.
High paddockcore and Extra-high depotcore hit the 3-hour bound and have no Code quality score; each level carries a second figure with the timeout counted as 0.

Two Muse Code versions: Low and 21 Medium runs on 1.4.6, the last two Medium runs, High and Extra-high on 1.4.9, which Meta released with a quota reset and which runs its reminder observers on Muse Spark 1.3.
Cost is an estimate at the Muse Wonder 1.0 list price; Meta publishes no price for Muse Wonder Full.

Contributor mode: Meta may train on submitted content, so Frontier v4 task content may enter future Meta training data. The owner accepted this. Max is not offered in Contributor mode, so these are all the levels.

The per-minute overlap log recorded another local benchmark process during 9 Medium, 14 High and 5 Extra-high runs (overlap_minutes_logged); this can lengthen minutes, and Extra-high depotcore hit the 3-hour limit with 145 of its 180 minutes overlapped, so its timeout may be partly due to the load. A clean rerun is scheduled after the 2026-10-19 Muse quota reset. The log started with Medium.
One High snapcore attempt stopped on a Meta API transport error 8 minutes in; it is unscored and kept apart, and the task was rerun.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.
One attempt per task and level, on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound.
publication_scope: Per-run scores, per-panel sub-scores, aggregates, judge protocol text, calibration verdicts and control means, integrity-audit verdicts, raw tokens, model calls by model, the estimated cost and the logged overlap minutes.
withheld: quirk answer keys (they describe hidden-test behaviour)
reviewer session identifiers and usage receipts
integrity_limit: Hash checks bind the export to frozen files; they do not prove that judges were unbiased or that no training overlap exists.
